So often the entire relationship is based on sexual desire, infatuation, and "chemistry" rather than on things like friendship, commitment, sacrificial love, or devotion. And they only ever portray romance as candlelight dinners, bouquets of flowers, grand gestures and beautiful moments.

Being attracted to your spouse, enjoying their company, feeling passion for one another - these are important. I don't believe any of us should go into marriage expecting that there is a "honeymoon period" that will pass and that our relationship will eventually become old hat. That guarantees that your relationship will become old hat! But your relationship needs to be based on more than attraction...if it isn't built around a solid friendship, you're gonna have a bad time. If you want the attraction and passion and delight in one another's company to last, you have to work on that. You have to set aside time for one another, keep on flirting with each other, put effort into maintaining your looks and a healthy weight, and most importantly be brave enough to name, face, and deal with your problems together. And you have to learn how to see romance differently - flowers and intimate dinners are lovely, but there is also romance in a husband getting up at 5 a.m. to bring a hungry baby into bed so his wife won't have to get up to nurse, or in a wife going camping with her husband for years even though she hates it because it's something he loves to do. Love isn't only expressed in Hallmark moments; it's also shown in the little nitty-gritty moments we live out through the years, the acts of sacrifice and tenderness that you could easily overlook in the hustle and bustle of daily life.

Anyway. So yeah. Hollywood's portrayal of romance gets it all wrong. Romantic marriage is delightful and entirely attainable, just not if you do things Hollywood's way.
